samples.explanation: A real revolute joint brings the separated lever pivot onto the grounded base pivot.
The real as-built hinge is created in the existing placement. Its native pivot glyph is shown without moving either component.
The genuine named joint-origin triad is located on the lever pivot.
Driving the hinge changes the blue lever from zero to 45 degrees.
A new 30-degree upper limit clamps the actual lever from its former 70-degree pose.
The orange tip follows the blue lever as one rigid group during a hinge drive.
The actual free component is translated and rotated, preserving the grounded base.
The actual computed path of the lever tip is kept as a native 3D sketch spline, as in the Motion Trace dialog.
The saved exploded view is displayed using the native Explode view command.
The real study plays its keyed hinge from zero to 90 degrees.
Raised native index bars expose coupled rotations of +60 and -90 degrees, at the specified 12:8 radius ratio.
The same indexed wheels show a general motion link: +60 degrees drives +30 degrees.
Turning the indexed pinion by 45 degrees translates the orange rack by 10*pi/4 mm.
The native screw relation couples a 450-degree turn with 15 mm of axial travel; the nut is an asymmetric indexed block.
A half turn of the eccentric native disk moves the contacting knife follower 8 mm toward the center.
The native two-link reach solver moves the tip from its actual starting pose to the reachable point [25,25,10].
